in_text_mentions: The proband's niece is female who is 28 years old. She had no history of surgery in her both eyes. At present, she uses timolol, azopt, and alphagan to control IOP. Her IOP measured with Goldmann tonometry was 35 mmHg in the right eye and 36 mmHg in the left eye. Corectopia and peripheral anterior synechia were seen in the right eye, and iris hypoplasia, corectopia, polycoria, and peripheral anterior synechia were seen in the left eye (Figure 3). No systemic abnormalities was found. We advised her to have antiglaucoma surgery in both her eyes as soon as possible.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: OCT of patient II-1 (PITX2-deletion ARS) shows iris apposition to cornea and abnormal goniostrands reducing the iridocorneal angle—classic Axenfeld anomaly/iridocorneal adhesion features of ARS. B: Goniosynechiae with goniostrands severely narrowing the iridocorneal angle in ARS patient II-1, explaining the high IOP—classic gonioscopic iridocorneal tissue bands of ARS. C: OCT shows polycoria, iris hypoplasia remnant, and iridocorneal synechia—classic Rieger iris anomaly and polycoria of ARS. D: OCT demonstrates abnormal goniostrands and a partial iris-bridge remnant of hypoplasia—classic iris hypoplasia and gonioscopic band features of ARS.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a patient's abdomen showing a protruding/everted umbilicus with redundant periumbilical skin. The disease-focused article title (Axenfeld-Rieger Syndrome case) together with the specific captioned manifestation establishes attribution to axenfeld_rieger_syndrome; the in-text explicitly describes this as a manifestation of the case patient. The finding maps to the configured vocabulary entry for redundant periumbilical skin (synonym protruding umbilicus). It is a real patient image, not a diagram, control, other-disease panel, or third-party figure, and it is adequately lit. Umbilical involvement is a recognized but non-classic manifestation of ARS, so typicality is variant. No arrows or labels are present on the image. The caption and in-text mention do not state age or ethnicity, so those are left unknown; skin tone is judged from the visible abdominal skin.
